subject: Private Offer: Azure marketplace – federal procurement exhibit & billing flow
messages:
From: Emma Turner <procurement@heliosbank.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@heliosbank.com
Date: Fri, 19 Sep 2026 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Private Offer: Azure marketplace – federal procurement exhibit & billing flow

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this — Helios is evaluating private offers for a pilot (financial services, regulated) and we need the following to progress procurement/legal approvals: 

- A draft Entitlement Exhibit that maps Redwoods SKUs to Helios internal cost codes (we need this for our internal entitlements registry).
- Billing & invoicing flow (we require invoice to be sent to AP@heliosbank.com and a monthly consolidated invoice; PO-based billing, 30 days).
- Evidence for security/compliance: SOC 2 Type II report or SOC 2 supplement for the marketplace offering, and statement about where customer data is stored (US-only or EU options).
- Confirmation whether the private offer can include an explicit Federal procurement exhibit (Helios is on several state/federal frameworks and they require a short exhibit stating data residency controls).
- Microsoft contact for co-sell enablement and any marketplace provisioning steps that require Helios acceptance.

Can you share a draft exhibit + standard billing appendix we can share with our procurement and legal? We’d like to get a PO template over to you today if possible.

Regards,
Emma Turner
Senior Procurement Manager
Helios Bank

---
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Emma Turner <procurement@heliosbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2026 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer: Azure marketplace – federal procurement exhibit & billing flow

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear list. High level next steps from our side: 

1) I’m attaching a first-pass Entitlement Exhibit template (RI_PrivateOffer_Entitlement_Exhibit_v1.docx) and our standard billing appendix.
2) Ben (legal) will review the compliance/evidence language; we typically provide a SOC 2 supplement and a short data residency statement for marketplace private offers.
3) Marissa (sales ops) will coordinate PO handling and set up the consolidated invoice cadence you requested.
4) We’ll identify the Microsoft co-sell contact and outline the marketplace provisioning path (private offer activation vs. reserved capacity notes).

Can you attach your PO template and any internal entitlement mapping (cost center codes)? That will let us map SKUs to your ledger. Also want to flag: if you require FedRAMP-specific language we’ll need to route through our security & compliance team — we should know if the ask is FedRAMP-in-scope or a FedRAMP-equivalent attestation.

Attachments: RI_PrivateOffer_Entitlement_Exhibit_v1.docx, SOC2-Supplement.pdf

Best,
Irene Choi
Senior Account Executive — Marketplace Sales
Redwood Inference

---
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Emma Turner <procurement@heliosbank.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer: Azure marketplace – federal procurement exhibit & billing flow

Emma / Irene — quick legal read of the requested items and proposed language snippets below. This is a first pass; I’ve put bolded flags where Helios may want a minor concession.

1) Entitlement Exhibit (proposed):
"Redwood Inference will provide entitlements for the Private Offer as set forth in Exhibit A. Entitlements are non-transferable and will be invoiced per the Billing Appendix. Redwood will map Marketplace SKUs to Customer cost-codes upon receipt of Customer's completed entitlement mapping spreadsheet."

2) Billing & Invoicing (proposed):
"Invoices shall be issued monthly and sent to AP@heliosbank.com. Payment terms: Net 30 from invoice date. Disputes must be raised within 60 days of invoice receipt. For Marketplace Private Offers, Redwood may invoice Microsoft-reimbursed amounts separately when Microsoft remits co-sell credits (Helios will be credited accordingly)."

- Flag: If Helios requires Microsoft-managed invoicing only (i.e., Microsoft issues invoice and Redwood receives reimbursement), that changes the documentary flow and we’ll need to coordinate with Marketplace Ops.

3) Compliance evidence & audits:
"Redwood will provide SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and a supplemental attestation describing data residency. Redwood retains the right to redact sensitive infrastructure details but will provide proof of controls to support procurement review."

4) Federal procurement exhibit:
We can provide a short exhibit describing data residency and encryption-at-rest policies but cannot provide FedRAMP authorization unless explicitly stated; if Helios requires FedRAMP in-scope controls we need to escalate.

I’ll incorporate any specific PO terms Helios sends. Also copying Marissa to get the billing flow and DocuSign timeline.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Counsel, Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Emma Turner <procurement@heliosbank.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: Howard Lee <howard.lee@pivotlegal.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private Offer: Azure marketplace – federal procurement exhibit & billing flow

Ben / Irene — thanks, that language is helpful. A few follow-ups from procurement/legal: 

- Attached is our PO template (Helios_PO_Template.pdf). Please review: Helios requires the following billing block on invoices: "Helios Bank — AP Dept, 200 Market St, Invoice# [xxxx], PO#[yyyy]".
- We will send an entitlement mapping spreadsheet by end of day with cost center codes.
- Microsoft invoicing: we prefer Redwood to invoice Helios directly (Microsoft reimbursements are fine) but if Microsoft mandates marketplace-managed invoicing for co-sell credits, we will accept that provided we get a reconciliation report.
- For FedRAMP — Helios is not mandating FedRAMP for this pilot, but we do require a written exhibit describing data residency and encryption controls for internal auditors.

I’m copying our outside counsel Howard Lee (pivotlegal) who will review legal redlines.

Regards,
Emma

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private Offer: Azure marketplace – federal procurement exhibit & billing flow

Emma — appreciated. Operational notes and timeline from Redwood: 

- Marissa will own invoice routing and will configure our marketplace billing to include the Helios billing block. We will need the completed entitlement mapping spreadsheet to finalize SKU mapping (expected 1 business day after we receive the sheet).
- Legal redlines: Ben will provide a redline to the Entitlement Exhibit within 48 hours (Ben: planned deliverable by Friday EOD).
- Evidence: SOC2-Supplement.pdf attached. For anything requiring an NDA, we can move the SOC 2 file into a limited-access Drive folder (link below).
- Next steps: 1) Helios sends completed entitlement mapping + PO template (we received the PO template — thanks). 2) Redwood issues a DocuSign for the Entitlement Exhibit + Billing Appendix. 3) Upon execution, we will activate the private offer in the Azure Marketplace and provide the marketplace offer id and Microsoft co-sell contact.

Target timetable: Entitlement mapping + signed exhibit within 7 business days, marketplace activation within 3 business days after signature (subject to Microsoft processing).
